opening: We lint, format and interpret our shell scripts with this parser, formatter and interpreter (the syntax and interp packages), and several scripts are mishandled. The formatter runs with default options unless noted. These are three separate problems: none of them depends on another, and each can be fixed and checked on its own.

requirements.m01: The formatter prints a logical not in arithmetic with no space after it: (( ! 0 )) becomes ((!0)), and in an interactive shell with history expansion !0 is a history event, so the formatted script breaks there. A space should follow the ! in arithmetic expressions, except in minified output, which stays compact.
requirements.m02: With the parser's RecoverErrors option on, an unterminated deprecated arithmetic expansion such as "$[incomp" still fails with a hard error, while "$((incomp" is recovered. The bracket form should be recovered the same way: the parse succeeds, the expansion's closing position is marked as recovered, and exactly one missing piece is reported.
requirements.m03: The formatter moves a statement that follows another on the same line onto its own line even when the pair is deliberate: main "$@"; exit $? comes out as two lines. Shells read a script line by line while running it, so an exit guard that no longer shares a line with the command before it can misbehave, and a=$1; shift loses its intent the same way. When the source already has the two statements on one line and the second is a plain call to exit, return, shift, break or continue, they should stay on one line: main "$@"; exit $?, a=$1; shift, foo; return $?, foo; break, foo; continue, foo; ! exit 1, foo & exit 1, and cat <<DOC; exit 1 followed by its heredoc body must all format unchanged. Only that pair stays joined: foo; exit 1; bar becomes foo; exit 1 with bar on the next line; if a; then b; exit 1; fi becomes if a; then on one line, an indented b; exit 1, then fi; foo || { echo err; exit 1; } becomes foo || { with an indented echo err; exit 1 and the closing brace on its own line; and in case $1 in with the branch -v) x=1; break ;; the x=1; break stays together on its indented line, with ;; on the next. Minified output and single-line output are not affected.
